title: Nudge payout sweeps full balance to caller-supplied recipient: deterministic frontrun, refill arbitrage, recipient asymmetry, and threshold gaming
rejection_rationale:
Mischaracterizes documented design as bugs. NatSpec at `BatchNFTMinter.sol#L18-22` explicitly documents that (1) the nudge "transfers its full balance" to `recipient` (balance-sweep is intended), (2) payout goes "to `recipient`" (caller-supplied recipient is intended), and (3) the qualifier is `count >= nudgeSize` with no scaling factor (no proportionality is intended).

- Vector A (mempool-race full-pool drain) reduces to legitimate competition for the documented winner-takes-pool design.
- Vector B (recipient asymmetry / wrapper extraction) is the standard router/aggregator pattern (`msg.sender` pays, `recipient` receives — same as Uniswap/1inch); the wrapper framing is user-approval phishing, a C4 invalid pattern.
- Vector C (threshold gaming across refills) is Vector A repeated across refill cycles.

User feedback (2026-05-06) confirmed both core premises are intentional design.
rootCause: The nudge payout is computed as `IERC20(nudgePaymentToken).balanceOf(address(this))` and transferred to a caller-supplied `recipient` whenever `count >= nudgeSize`. Three structural decisions compound: (1) the payout is the entire current contract balance rather than a per-batch cap, (2) the qualifying threshold is a simple inequality with no proportional scaling, and (3) the recipient is decoupled from `msg.sender`. Together these turn every refill of the nudge pool into a deterministic public-mempool race won by whoever pays for the cheapest qualifying batch (`count == nudgeSize`) with the highest priority fee.
consolidatedDescription:
All raw findings in this cluster are surface manifestations of the same broken invariant: the nudge pool has no per-claim limit, no commit-reveal gating, no claimer/payer link, and no scaling with batch size. Specifically:

(A) FRONTRUN A FUNDED BALANCE (CODE-003 / ECON-002 frontrun variant) - Once the yield funnel deposits NUDGE into the contract, any MEV searcher can submit a `batchMint` with the minimum qualifying `count` and `recipient = themselves`, sweeping the entire pool ahead of the legitimate large-batch user the funnel was meant to incentivize.

(B) MEMPOOL-OBSERVABLE REFILL ARBITRAGE (ECON-001 / ECON-003) - Every owner refill (`IERC20.transfer(batchMinter, X)`) is publicly visible. Searchers bundle a `batchMint(count == nudgeSize, recipient = searcher)` immediately behind every refill via Flashbots, draining the freshly-funded pool atomically.

(C) RECIPIENT != msg.sender ASYMMETRY (ECON-002 / CODE-003) - `paymentAmount` is pulled from `msg.sender` and the dust refund is returned to `msg.sender`, but the nudge transfer goes to `recipient`. A malicious frontend can silently inject its own address as `recipient` while still routing the NFTs through a wrapper, capturing nudges from naive users. Independently, the asymmetry is what makes the frontrun in (A) cheap.

(D) THRESHOLD GAMING (ECON-004) - The check is `count >= nudgeSize`, with full-balance payout. This dis-incentivizes batches above the threshold (a batch of 1000 earns the same nudge as a batch of `nudgeSize`), so rational actors converge on the cheapest qualifying batch.

(E) RECIPIENT-AS-PROTOCOL-CONTRACT GRIEFING (ECON-010) - The same recipient-asymmetry lets anyone set `recipient = NFTStaker` (or any protocol contract), permanently stranding both the minted NFTs and the nudge tokens in a contract with no rescue path.
exploitScenarioCanonical:
1. Yield funnel transfers 50,000 USDC to BatchNFTMinter (nudgeSize=5, paymentToken=phUSD).
2. Searcher monitors mempool, detects the inbound transfer.
3. Searcher constructs Flashbots bundle: [funnel_transfer (already pending), batchMint(count=5, recipient=searcher, paymentAmount=cost(5)_phUSD)].
4. Bundle lands. Searcher pays ~5,000 phUSD (recoverable in part as NFT value or by re-selling), receives 50,000 USDC + 5 NFTs. Net profit ~45,000 USDC per cycle.
5. Legitimate large-batch user (Alice, count=1000) submits her tx after the searcher's bundle lands. Her batch sees `balanceOf(batchMinter) == 0` and pays no nudge. She has paid for 1000 mints with no incentive - exactly the scenario the funnel was trying to prevent.
6. Repeats every refill.
impactSummary: Direct theft of all owner-funded incentive budget on every refill cycle. Legitimate batch-minters, who are the intended beneficiaries, structurally cannot win the race against a searcher bot. The yield funnel becomes a one-way faucet to MEV searchers.
unionOfMitigations: Pay a fixed owner-configured `nudgePerBatch` amount per qualifying batch rather than the full balance, so the pool drains over many batches and a single frontrun captures only one batch's worth.
Make the payout proportional to count: `nudgePerBatch * count / nudgeSize` capped at balance - aligns the incentive with batch size and removes the threshold-gaming cliff.
Require `recipient == msg.sender` so the nudge accrues to the actual payer; closes the malicious-frontend gift-extraction vector and the recipient-as-protocol-contract grief.
Implement a drip schedule: track `lastNudgeBlock` and only allow nudges up to a per-block dripped amount.
Allowlist a known yield-funnel-controlled distributor as the only address authorized to claim nudges.

Combine refill with distribution atomically: have the funnel call a single `refillAndDistribute(...)` entrypoint that funds the pool and pays out to a deterministic set of recipients in the same tx (or via commit-reveal), eliminating the mempool reaction window.
preservedDetails: ECON-001 has the strongest economic profitability calculation. CODE-003 has the cleanest frontrun walkthrough. ECON-002 has the recipient-asymmetry analysis. ECON-003 has the Flashbots bundle construction. ECON-004 has the threshold-gaming variants. ECON-010 has the cross-contract griefing into NFTStaker.

classification.justification: Meets C4 High criteria: 'Assets can be stolen/lost/compromised directly or via a valid attack path that does not have hand-wavy hypotheticals.' The owner-funded nudge pool is a real asset (USDC/external incentive budget). The attack path is concrete: (i) refill is publicly visible in mempool, (ii) Flashbots bundle construction is standard MEV infrastructure, (iii) `count == nudgeSize` minimizes attacker cost, (iv) caller-supplied `recipient` lets the attacker keep the NFTs. No hypothetical conditions: any externally-funded refill on mainnet is structurally exposed. Independently, ECON-010 (recipient = NFTStaker) is a clean permanent-loss path on misuse. The protocol's stated intent (NatSpec lines 19-22, 'incentivize batch-minting via an externally-funded pool') is unreachable in adversarial conditions, so 'first qualifying caller wins' is NOT the intended design - the nudge is meant to subsidize legitimate large-batch users, who are structurally outraced by searchers.
preconditions: Owner has configured nudgeSize > 0 and nudgePaymentToken != address(0).
An external funder (yield funnel, owner) has transferred nudgePaymentToken into BatchNFTMinter.

Attacker has phUSD (or whatever paymentToken the dispatcher requires) in an amount sufficient for cost(nudgeSize) mints. For nudgeSize=5 at startPrice=1000 phUSD this is ~5K phUSD - a trivially small capital requirement relative to nudge sizes large enough to actually nudge behaviour.
guardrails_observed: Up-front guard `nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken` prevents the dust refund and the nudge from sharing a token (incidentally protects the single-dispatcher production wiring against rewardToken collision; see L-04).
DUST_THRESHOLD sweep returns surplus payment to msg.sender (caller is not griefed on payment surplus).
Approval is revoked at end of mint loop (line 135), reducing residual allowance attack surface for non-reentrant exits.
classification.guardrails_insufficient_because: None of the existing guardrails address the fundamental issues: balance-sweep payout, recipient != msg.sender, threshold-gaming. The mempool race exists for any mainnet deployment regardless of owner trust assumptions.
classification.asset_at_risk: The full nudgePaymentToken balance held by BatchNFTMinter at any time. In production this is owner- or yield-funnel-supplied USDC (or analogous external incentive token). Any refill is fully drainable.
